what: Labelled set for insertion #4 (PER-COMMAND DRIFT) of docs/jev-integration-plan.md's second-wave table.
how: 30 commands taken verbatim from tools/hooks/material_marker.log (the gate's own record of every command that
RUNS a recipe or bench script), paired with the `## NEXT` FIRST ACT that was in force when they ran.
The three windows are delimited by the STATUS.md commits that rewrote NEXT; the first act is re-extracted
from git at trial time (`git show <sha>:STATUS.md`), so the set cannot drift from the document.
LABELLING RULE, applied strictly and stated because it bounds the result: on-task = the command advances the
FIRST ACT as written. A later act that the SAME hand-off defers ('THEN D-2 ...') is labelled off-task, and so
is machinery work (tool self-tests, audit repairs). That is the literal question the gate asks; the cost of
the framing is measured in the trial's `sequel` breakdown rather than argued about.
Labelled by the material session of 2026-09-22 from the logs each command produced.
